title: test(types): the parity docblock names its instrument instead of restating its count (objectui#9603)
body:
Fixes #9603

Clause-②: no

## The defect

`zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` carried a docblock clause that RESTATED a live figure — the `Tests N passed (N)` line vitest prints for this file — and the figure had rotted. `AGENTS.md` #9 forbids exactly that: point at the instrument that re-derives a claim, and never write down its answer.

⭐ The irony is the finding, not decoration. This is the file whose entire job is to stop a hand-written restatement drifting away from what it restates, and it carried that defect in its own prose.

## Both numbers re-measured here, not taken from the card

| probe | reading | instrument |
|---|---|---|
| the quoted figure | **12** | the literal in the clause |
| what the runtime half actually prints | **`Tests 37 passed (37)`** | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` at `4b577229` |
| static cross-check, `it(` / `test(` at line start | **37** | agrees with the instrument |
| ⭐ lit control — is the probe reading this file at all | `describe(` → **12** hits | connected |
| ⭐ negative control | `Tests 999999 passed` → **0** | does not fire spuriously |

⚠️ **The card's own replacement number was already stale by the time this was dispatched.** The filing seat measured **32** on `origin/main` on 2026-09-16; the instrument prints **37** at `4b577229` on 2026-09-18. Two days, five cases. That reading is what decided the shape below — it is evidence, not taste.

## Which shape, and why it is the right one for a file with THIS job

**Chosen: remove the restated figure.** ⛔ Not "update the figure to 37".

1. **A replacement number buys about one merge.** 12 → 32 → 37 inside the life of a single card. Writing `37` would have re-created the defect with a fresher number and handed the next reader the same trap, in the file least able to afford it.
2. ⭐ **A restated case count in THIS file rots on GOOD NEWS.** The suite grows whenever someone adds a pin — which is this file working. So the figure is not merely at risk of going stale; it is guaranteed to, and it goes stale precisely when the file succeeds. Diligence cannot make it durable. Deleting it can.
3. ⭐ **The figure-free spelling was already in the file, and it had never rotted.** Thirty lines below, the sibling `WiderLedgerMismatch` clause makes the same claim about the same instrument — "their passing test counts do not move when this reddens" — carrying no number. That is `AGENTS.md` #9 already applied once, by this file's own author, to this file's own sentence. Restating the count in one clause while naming the instrument in its sibling was the whole defect, visible on one screen.
4. Precedent points the same way: objectui#9617 took this route for the same class of rot elsewhere in this repo ("the count is ten, and derived rather than restated"), and PR objectui#9872 has just taken it for a published docblock.

**The card's option 2 — pin it — was considered and rejected on cost.** The number is vitest's own output; no in-file constant can read it. A pin would have to assert the suite's own case count, so it would redden on every legitimate test addition. A ratchet that fires on good news is the defect restated as machinery, not a remedy.

## What was deliberately NOT touched

This file's header splits a docblock **by CLAUSE**: a clause that RECORDS a measurement is historical and ⛔ may never be rewritten by a later card; a clause that GIVES GUIDANCE must be true now, and a later card MAY and MUST amend it, naming the card that moved it.

- The restated figure sat in the **guidance** half ("... does not move when this half reddens, correctly"). Amending it is therefore obligatory rather than merely permitted, and the new text names objectui#9603 as the header requires.
- The two **record** clauses beside it — "it did not move under the ablation either", and the parenthetical reading `5 passed (5)` until objectui#6705 added the seven-fixture suite — are left **byte-identical**; the diff renders them as unchanged context lines.
- ⛔ **No assertion, ledger entry, ledger key, or runtime behaviour changed.** What the test asserts was out of bounds for this card.

⚠️ **One correction to the card's reasoning; it does not change the outcome.** The card read the whole sentence as a RECORD clause and concluded that this file's own ruling barred an in-place repair. Judged by clause, as that ruling requires, the rotten figure is in the guidance half and the record half is the adjacent parenthetical. The card's conclusion still stands, but on its other ground — the choice between deleting and pinning was a judgement, not a mechanical substitution.

## The figures the new prose does carry, and why they cannot rot

The replacement clause writes 12, 32 and 37. Each is anchored to a named past event — "true when objectui#6705 wrote it", "when the card was filed", "at `4b577229`" — which is the HISTORICAL form the header explicitly permits: readings of a tree that is fixed.

⚠️ Stated honestly, as the card did about its own scope: nothing PINS this clause. `headerFigures()` guards the header's ledger figures only, and this clause sits about a thousand lines below the header. That is the whole point of removing the live figure rather than refreshing it — a historical figure needs no guard; a live one in an unguarded clause is the defect being repaired.

## Verification

All runs at `a8c07118`, on a worktree byte-identical to HEAD. ⚠️ Exit codes were captured by redirecting to a file first, never read across a pipe.

| check | command | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| target suite | `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/zod-mirror-parity.test.ts` | exit 0 — `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 37 passed (37)` |
| package type-check | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check` | exit 0, echoing `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` — so the compile-time assertions in this file were actually read |
| package lint | `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types lint` | exit 0 — 0 errors, 290 pre-existing warnings |
| changeset presence | `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — one changeset, EMPTY frontmatter, the explicit test-only exemption |
| changeset no-major | `node scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs` | exit 0 |
| changeset claims | `node scripts/check-changeset-claims.mjs` | exit 0 |
| pending changeset literals | `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | exit 0 |
| control bytes | `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — 7952 tracked text files scanned |
| line citations | `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | exit 0 — **0 new** cross-file line citations |
| test path roots | `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | exit 0 |

**Does any citation move?** ⛔ No. `git grep -nE 'zod-mirror-parity\.test\.ts:[0-9]+'` over the whole tree returns nothing: no file anywhere cites this one by line address, so a twelve-line insertion at about 3370 moves no pointer. The cross-file mentions that do exist are all in `.changeset/*.md` and cite this file by filename and symbol, which is `AGENTS.md` #11's required form.

**Repo-wide lint, declared as a measured narrowing rather than skipped.** `eslint . --no-inline-config --format json` reports a universe of **5104** files — read from eslint's own config, not assumed — of which **79** carry errors; this file is **not** among them, and its own targeted run is 0 errors with 2 pre-existing `no-explicit-any` warnings, both far above the diff. Invariance: `eslint.config.js` declares no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project`, so type-aware linting is off and this diff cannot move the verdict on any untouched file.

### The file's figure-guard is live — proved, then reverted

Since the new prose still carries figures, it is worth knowing whether anything here can catch a duplicate. One-shot ablation, run against the committed tree:

- **Mutation** — a second copy of one pinned header spelling injected on disk; the occurrence count was verified **1 → 2 on disk** before anything was run, so the ablation is known to have landed rather than assumed.
- **Result** — exit 1, `Tests 2 failed | 35 passed (37)`, both failures naming the guard verbatim:

```
AssertionError: the header spelling /\*\*(\d+) entries\*\* in `RuntimeOnlyDeclared`/
must occur exactly once in .../zod-mirror-parity.test.ts; it occurs 2 times:
expected 2 to be 1
```

- **Restore** — verified by byte identity, ⛔ not by an exit code: on-disk `git hash-object` equals the HEAD blob (`cb3d5f08...`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the ablation marker greps to 0. A `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM using absolute paths covered the crash path.

⇒ the guard exists and it fires, and it covers the header — which is exactly why the clause a thousand lines below it needed its figure removed rather than refreshed.

## Acceptance notes

**No sibling instance of this defect class remains in the file** — swept rather than assumed. The only other `N passed` figures sit in the objectui#6058 ablation record, which is anchored to a named card and written in the past tense (HISTORICAL, and ⛔ not to be rewritten), and the two "**85 keys** ... today" clauses are both pinned by `headerFigures()` at the runtime leg. The repaired clause was the only unpinned live one.

**Labels.** ⚠️ In this repo labelling is CI-owned and destructive: `.github/workflows/labeler.yml` runs `actions/labeler` on `opened` / `synchronize` / `reopened`, and that action applies its whole set in ONE `setLabels` call, which REPLACES rather than adds. `.github/labeler.yml` derives `package: types` and `tests` from these paths. An additive write from this seat would therefore be silently clobbered by the next sync, so none was made; the label set is reported as read back in the delivery report instead.

Out of scope, noted and ⛔ not filed:

- The card's own title cites this file as a `path:line` address, and that address is already false — the line it names reads 3371 today. `AGENTS.md` #11 bans cross-file line addresses, but its carrier list is comments, assertions, failure messages, docs, changesets and script headers; an issue title is not among them, and `check:new-line-citations` scans tracked files only. So this is a live illustration of why the ban exists rather than a breach of it. Carrier: the next seat editing that card — and if none comes, none is needed.

⛔ Nothing filed under the three classes: no reproducible defect, no other declared contract measured false, and no trap that would lead an author to write metadata the runtime rejects or silently drops.
